scenarios.title: Repair client access using listener and scan evidence
scenarios.summary: Distinguish a filtered service from an absent listener, then repair the whole client-range policy.
scenarios.objective: On virtual server 198.51.100.20, keep TCP ports 22, 443 and 9000 reachable for the whole Admin range 10.20.0.0/24. For the whole Public range 10.30.0.0/24, keep 443 reachable but filter 22 and 9000. A single displayed client address is not the whole range. Keep diagnostic TCP 80 reachable enough to report closed from both observer positions; no service should be started there. Preserve all supplied processes and listener owners. Repair the current host filter, then Check configuration.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare ss with both observer views. A filtered connection is inconclusive about whether a listener exists; a blanket drop also breaks required access.
steps: Separate local listeners from client access
Repair the policy and retest the range

guide.title: Separate local listeners from client access
guide.why: ss describes supplied sockets; it does not establish whether a remote connection reaches them. The first INPUT decision may block a healthy listener.
guide.action: In Server terminal run ss -lntp and iptables -S INPUT. Note which client range the existing SSH drop names.

commands.explanation: Run this in the simulated Server terminal; it never operates on host services.
Run this in the simulated Server terminal; it never operates on host services.

guide.title: Compare the two observer positions
guide.why: Open means a modeled connection can reach a retained listener. Closed has a response without a listener. Filtered cannot tell whether the listener exists.
guide.action: In Observer terminal select Admin and run nmap -n -Pn -sT -p 22,80,443,9000 192.0.2.10. Select Public and repeat. Compare TCP 22 with 22 in ss, and contrast it with the closed 80 diagnostic.

commands.explanation: Run this in Observer terminal; the selected viewpoint supplies its source address.

guide.title: Repair the policy and retest the range
guide.why: The example uses Admin 10.50.0.0/24 and Public 10.60.0.0/24. Correct the range decision; avoid a rule for only one displayed client.
guide.action: In Server terminal remove the wrong first rule with iptables -D INPUT 1. Add Public-range drops for TCP 22 and 9000. Repeat both scans and choose Check example. Then try the independent assignment.

scenarios.explanation: The server already has a valid SSH listener; the initial Admin failure is caused by its INPUT policy. Remove or override the wrong source-range decision, filter Public SSH and preview traffic, and preserve Admin access plus HTTPS from both ranges. The deliberately permitted diagnostic port80 has no listener and therefore reports closed. INPUT and OUTPUT both affect the result; successful displayed samples do not establish the policy for an entire /24. Equivalent supported rule arrangements and prefix partitions are accepted.
hints: A TCP 22 listener already exists. Compare its local socket evidence with the rule source and the selected observer.
The existing SSH drop applies to the wrong client range. Rule order and the entire source prefix matter.
Keep the unused 80 diagnostic conclusively closed while preserving the real Admin services. Denying everything cannot satisfy the useful-access requirements.
scenarios.simplifications: Only one supplied IPv4 server and two declared reachable observation paths. Numeric TCP connect observations use fixed simulated source port 40000 and the host INPUT/OUTPUT filter plus supplied process/listener metadata. No real Nmap, packets, discovery, DNS, version detection, vulnerability inference, queues, application health, IDS or host actions. Current rules resume as saved exercise state; server boot persistence is a separate topic.

scenarios.title: Retire an exposed listener without taking down the useful services
scenarios.summary: Correlate socket owners, retire only the wildcard preview and verify both client views.
scenarios.objective: Retire the owner of the unused wildcard TCP 9000 preview. A paused owner or a firewall-only concealment is insufficient. Preserve the loopback-only preview on TCP 9001 and every approved owner, including SSH and HTTPS. Keep SSH on TCP 22 reachable for Admin clients 10.20.0.0/24 and filtered for Public clients 10.30.0.0/24; HTTPS on 443 must work from both ranges. TCP 9000 must no longer be open from either observer; closed or filtered is acceptable after its actual owner has ended.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Use the socket bind address and owning process together. Blocking a port and ending its owner are different repairs.

guide.title: Correlate the two preview instances
guide.why: A shared process name does not identify which bind is exposed. The existing listener lesson explains addresses and signal behavior.
guide.action: In Server terminal run ss -lntp and pgrep -x previewd. Identify the wildcard 9000 owner separately from the loopback 9001 owner.

guide.title: Observe the current exposure
guide.why: The selected observer sees a connection result, not a full application health or vulnerability report.
guide.action: In Observer terminal run nmap -n -Pn -sT -p 22,80,443,9000 192.0.2.10 from Admin, then select Public and run it again. Note that 9000 is open from both positions.

guide.title: Retire only the exposed instance
guide.why: Ending a process removes its supplied sockets; pausing or filtering it does not prove retirement.
guide.action: In the example only, run kill -TERM 110. Scan again from both observer positions, then Check example. Try STOP instead after a reset to see why it is insufficient.

scenarios.explanation: The wildcard preview owner is the retired component; the same-name loopback process must remain unchanged. Ending only the correct owner removes its retained listener. A filter alone may hide an open listener, while STOP leaves its socket present. Verify required SSH/HTTPS access from both client ranges as well as the preview being closed or filtered. Supported TERM, INT and KILL approaches are accepted when all required owners and policies remain correct.
hints: A process name can identify more than one instance. Match the wildcard 9000 listener to its owner.
ss -lntp identifies socket ownership; pgrep -x previewd alone does not distinguish the two instances.
A paused owner retains its listener. End only the intended owner, preserve the loopback instance, then check both observer views.
